<p id="mwHw">While the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bassa_Nge" title="Bassa Nge" class="mw-redirect" id="mwIA">Bassa Nge</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoruba_people" title="Yoruba people" id="mwIQ">Yoruba</a> (primarily the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oworo_people" title="Oworo people" id="mwIg">Oworo</a>, who are a subgroup of the Yoruba) and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nupe_people" title="Nupe people" id="mwIw">Nupe</a><sup about="#mwt25" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_4-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-:1-4"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:1-4" id="mwJA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwJQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJg">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwJw">]</span></span></a></sup> are indigenous to the area, other ethnic groups in Nigeria, including the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kupa_language" title="Kupa language" id="mwKA">Kupa-Nupe</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hausa_people" title="Hausa people" id="mwKQ">Hausa</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebira" title="Ebira" class="mw-redirect" id="mwKg">Ebira</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igala_people" title="Igala people" id="mwKw">Igala</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igbo_people" title="Igbo people" id="mwLA">Igbo</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bini_people" title="Bini people" class="mw-redirect" id="mwLQ">Bini/Edo</a>, and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiv_people" title="Tiv people" id="mwLg">Tiv</a><sup about="#mwt26" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:1_4-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":1"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:1-4" id="mwLw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwMA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMQ">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwMg">]</span></span></a></sup> have recently established themselves. Lokoja is projected to be the third fastest growing city on the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa" title="Africa" id="mwMw">African</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent" title="Continent" id="mwNA">continent</a> between 2020 and 2025, with a 5.93% growth rate.<sup about="#mwt29" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-5" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-5"}}"><a href="#cite_note-5" id="mwNQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwNg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwNw">[</span>5<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOA">]</span></span></a></sup><sup about="#mwt32" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-History_6-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"History"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-History-6"}}"><a href="#cite_note-History-6" id="mwOQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwOg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwOw">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwPA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwPQ">It was listed as a second class township by the 1917 <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Township" title="Township" id="mwPg">township</a> ordinance of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony" title="Colony" id="mwPw">colonial</a> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_administration" title="Public administration" id="mwQA">administration</a>, indicating that Lokoja is an old city.<sup about="#mwt35" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_7-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-:0-7"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-7" id="mwQQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwQg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwQw">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwRA">]</span></span></a></sup> Lokoja was founded in 1857 by <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Balfour_Baikie" title="William Balfour Baikie" id="mwRQ">William Balfour Baikie</a>, a British explorer, who established a trading post on the banks of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger_River" title="Niger River" id="mwRg">Niger River</a>. The city's strategic location made it an important center for trade and commerce in the region. Lokoja is a city with a rich history, cultural significance, and economic importance. Its strategic location and natural beauty make it a popular destination for tourists and investors alike.</p>

<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" id="mwRw" data-mw="{"autoGenerated":true}"></section><section data-mw-section-id="1" id="mwSA" aria-labelledby="Etymology"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Etymology">Etymology</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Lokoja&action=edit&section=1" title="Edit section: Etymology"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwSQ">Different ethnic groups lay claim to having named the city.</p>

<ul id="mwSg"><li id="mwSw">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoruba_people" title="Yoruba people" id="mwTA">Yoruba</a> (<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oworo_people" title="Oworo people" id="mwTQ">Oworo</a>) phrase; <i id="mwTg">Ilu Oke Oja</i> ("The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketplace" title="Marketplace" id="mwTw">market</a> town/settlement located on the hill").<sup about="#mwt38" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-8" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-8"}}"><a href="#cite_note-8" id="mwUA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwUQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUg">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwUw">]</span></span></a></sup></li>
<li id="mwVA">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hausa_people" title="Hausa people" id="mwVQ">Hausas</a> believe the name comes from <i id="mwVg">Loko Ja</i> ("A red corner") and that the city was named by the emir of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zazzau_Emirate" title="Zazzau Emirate" class="mw-redirect" id="mwVw">Zazzau</a>.<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt39" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwWA" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"citation needed","href":"./Template:Citation_needed"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"June 2024"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_June_2024" about="#mwt39"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt39" id="mwWQ"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2024)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup></li>
<li id="mwWg">The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nupe_people" title="Nupe people" id="mwWw">Nupes</a> believe the name comes from <i id="mwXA">Patti Lukongi</i> ("The hill of doves").<link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:All_articles_with_unsourced_statements" about="#mwt40" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwXQ" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"citation needed","href":"./Template:Citation_needed"},"params":{"date":{"wt":"June 2024"}},"i":0}}]}"><link rel="mw:PageProp/Category" href="./Category:Articles_with_unsourced_statements_from_June_2024" about="#mwt40"><sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;" about="#mwt40" id="mwXg"><span typeof="mw:Entity">[</span><i><a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2024)">citation needed</span></a></i><span typeof="mw:Entity">]</span></sup></li></ul>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="2" id="mwXw" aria-labelledby="History"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="History">History</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Lokoja&action=edit&section=2" title="Edit section: History"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwYA">The area that would become Lokoja has been inhabited for hundreds of years by people from different ethnic groups prior to the arrival of Europeans. The migrations of these groups to the area could be in part accounted for by its nearness to the banks of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger_River" title="Niger River" id="mwYQ">Niger</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benue_River" title="Benue River" id="mwYg">Benue</a> rivers. Some of the first groups of people to have settled in Lokoja were the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nupe_people" title="Nupe people" id="mwYw">Nupe groups</a> from Gbara near Bida, They are believed to have settled in Mount Patti, which is the settlement of the earliest inhabitants of Lokoja. The <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kupa_language" title="Kupa language" id="mwZA">Kupa</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kakanda_language" title="Kakanda language" id="mwZQ">Kakandas</a> are said to have migrated downstream the Niger from the town of Baro and other parts of present-day <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger_State" title="Niger State" id="mwZg">Niger State</a> to the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers, Oworo people/<a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoruba_people" title="Yoruba people" id="mwZw">Yoruba</a> from <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ile-Ife" title="Ile-Ife" class="mw-redirect" id="mwaA">Ile-Ife</a> joined in later.<sup about="#mwt41" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-History_6-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"History"}}"><a href="#cite_note-History-6" id="mwaQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwag"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwaw">[</span>6<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbA">]</span></span></a></sup> This area eventually became a center of trade.<sup about="#mwt44" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-9" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-9"}}"><a href="#cite_note-9" id="mwbQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwbg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwbw">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwcA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwcQ"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:River_Niger_at_Lokoja.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwcg"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:River_Niger_at_Lokoja.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/River_Niger_at_Lokoja.jpg/500px-River_Niger_at_Lokoja.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/River_Niger_at_Lokoja.jpg/960px-River_Niger_at_Lokoja.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3072" data-file-height="1728" data-file-type="bitmap" height="197" width="350" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.4" id="mwcw"></a><figcaption id="mwdA">River Niger at Lokoja</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwdQ">The Nupe and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zazzau_Emirate" title="Zazzau Emirate" class="mw-redirect" id="mwdg">Zazzau</a> emirs historically appointed the Hausas as political leaders, while the Nupe filled the position of religious leader as chief imam of Lokoja. Lokoja was ruled by the following Maigari of Lokoja: Hamza, Dauda, Musa, Muhammadu Maikarfi. The British then installed a Muslim convert called Bukar (originally named Abigel), who designated his residence at Yaragi Madabo Junction of Lokoja as the new Lokoja palace. In time, the position fell to Alhaji Yahaya Muhammadu Maikarfi, and after his <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demise" title="Demise" id="mwdw">demise</a>, Alhaji Kabiru, his son, succeeded him. The people sustained themselves by engaging in farming and hunting activities at Agbaja hill. Lokoja has an abundance of hills which were popular for hunting. At Mount Patti ("Patti" being the Nupe word for hill), there is a tree where the names of hunters were recorded in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajami" title="Ajami" class="mw-redirect" id="mweA">Ajami</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_script" title="Latin script" id="mweQ">Latin script</a>. 
When Dr <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Balfour_Baikie" title="William Balfour Baikie" id="mweg">William Balfour Baikie</a> arrived at Lokoja first in 1854 and later in 1857, he played a role in encouraging the outward movement of the people from their hilly settlements. He did this by influencing Muhammadu Maikarfi, then the Maigari of Lokoja. Muhammudu Maikarfi was then succeeded by Abigel (who converted to Islam and was renamed Bukar), who was widely seen as a stooge of the British.<sup about="#mwt47" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-10" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-10"}}"><a href="#cite_note-10" id="mwew"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwfA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfQ">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwfg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<p id="mwfw">The Bassa-Nges believe that they settled at the foot of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Patti" title="Mount Patti" id="mwgA">Mount Patti</a> when they came into Lokoja, before later moving again and migrating to settle across the Benue, just to the north of the Igalas. These different groups lived in different quarters of the town but were closely related socio-politically. They interacted freely and tolerated one another. Present day Lokoja is ruled by the <i id="mwgQ">Maigari</i> (chief) of Lokoja, and his 12 <i id="mwgg">Hakimi</i> (Sub chiefs). Each group have their own local spheres of control: for example, the Maigari has no jurisdiction over the Olu of Oworo (whose traditional jurisdiction begins from Felele), but he does have authority over Ganaja, Kwakware, Sarkin Numa, Adankolo, ward A to ward E and other villages of Lokoja urban.</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwgw"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lokoja-1911.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwhA"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lokoja-1911.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Lokoja-1911.jpg/500px-Lokoja-1911.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3e/Lokoja-1911.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled 2x" data-file-width="760" data-file-height="496" data-file-type="bitmap" height="228" width="350" class="mw-file-element mw-file-upright" style="--mw-file-upright: 1.4" id="mwhQ"></a><figcaption id="mwhg">Lokoja town in 1911</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mwhw">The present modern <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_settlement" title="Human settlement" id="mwiA">settlement</a> at Lokoja was established in 1857 by the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland" title="United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland" id="mwiQ">British</a> explorer <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Balfour_Baikie" title="William Balfour Baikie" id="mwig">William Baikie</a> at the site of an earlier model farm constructed during the failed <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger_expedition_of_1841" title="Niger expedition of 1841" id="mwiw">Niger expedition of 1841</a>. Lokoja was the capital of the British <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Nigeria_Protectorate" title="Northern Nigeria Protectorate" id="mwjA">Northern Nigeria Protectorate</a> and the chief of Lokoja at that time was Alhaji Muhammadu Maikarfi. Lokoja remained a convenient administrative town for the British colonial government after the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amalgamation_(politics)" title="Amalgamation (politics)" class="mw-redirect" id="mwjQ">amalgamation</a> of Northern and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Nigeria_Protectorate" title="Southern Nigeria Protectorate" id="mwjg">Southern Nigeria</a> in 1914.<sup about="#mwt50" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-11" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-11"}}"><a href="#cite_note-11" id="mwjw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwkA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwkQ">[</span>11<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwkg">]</span></span></a></sup> The first <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Governors-General_of_Nigeria" title="List of Governors-General of Nigeria" class="mw-redirect" id="mwkw">Governor-General</a>, Sir <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lugard" title="Frederick Lugard" class="mw-redirect" id="mwlA">Frederick Lugard</a>, governed the new nation of Nigeria from Lokoja. Other subsequent settlers into the city include the Yoruba (mainstream), the Igala, the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebira_people" title="Ebira people" id="mwlQ">Ebira</a> (Ebira Tao and Igbira Koto), and the Bassa-Nge people. However, there are other groups apart from the ones mentioned above but they are classified as temporary visitors and non indigenous. These include the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igbo_people" title="Igbo people" id="mwlg">Igbo</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiv_people" title="Tiv people" id="mwlw">Tiv</a>, <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bini_people" title="Bini people" class="mw-redirect" id="mwmA">Edo</a>, etc.</p>

<p id="mwmQ">The city's population has since grown to an estimated count of over 90,000 inhabitants.<sup about="#mwt53" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-12" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-12"}}"><a href="#cite_note-12" id="mwmg"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwmw"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnA">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwnQ">]</span></span></a></sup> It is a trade center with respect to its agricultural products; this is because it is situated at the confluence of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niger_River" title="Niger River" id="mwng">Niger</a> and <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benue_River" title="Benue River" id="mwnw">Benue</a> rivers, and is close to the federal capital of Nigeria in <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abuja" title="Abuja" id="mwoA">Abuja</a>. It is also home to <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kogi_State_Polytechnic" title="Kogi State Polytechnic" id="mwoQ">Kogi State Polytechnic</a> and the newly established <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_University,_Lokoja" title="Federal University, Lokoja" id="mwog">Federal University Lokoja</a>.<sup about="#mwt56" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-13" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-13"}}"><a href="#cite_note-13" id="mwow"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwpA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpQ">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwpg">]</span></span></a></sup> The population of Lokoja is estimated at more than 265,000 people, as at 2022.<sup about="#mwt59" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-14" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-14"}}"><a href="#cite_note-14" id="mwpw"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwqA"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwqQ">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwqg">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="4" id="mwtQ" aria-labelledby="Geography"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Geography">Geography</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Lokoja&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Geography"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwtg"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lokoja_vegetation.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwtw"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lokoja_vegetation.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Lokoja_vegetation.jpg/250px-Lokoja_vegetation.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Lokoja_vegetation.jpg/500px-Lokoja_vegetation.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" alt="Lokoja Vegetation" data-file-width="3120" data-file-height="2083" data-file-type="bitmap" height="167" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwuA"></a><figcaption id="mwuQ">Lokoja vegetation</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mwug"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rain_forests_of_lokoja.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mwuw"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rain_forests_of_lokoja.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Rain_forests_of_lokoja.jpg/250px-Rain_forests_of_lokoja.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Rain_forests_of_lokoja.jpg/500px-Rain_forests_of_lokoja.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3077" data-file-height="1847" data-file-type="bitmap" height="150" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mwvA"></a><figcaption id="mwvQ">Grasses and trees in Lokoja</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mwvg">Lokoja lies about 7.8023° north of the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equator" title="Equator" id="mwvw">equator</a> and 6.7333° E east of the Meridian.<sup about="#mwt74" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-17" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-17"}}"><a href="#cite_note-17" id="mwwA"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwwQ"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwwg">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwww">]</span></span></a></sup> It is about 165<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwxA"> </span>km southwest of Abuja as the crow flies, and 390<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwxQ"> </span>km Northeast of <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagos" title="Lagos" id="mwxg">Lagos</a> by same measure. Residential districts are of varying density, and the city has various suburbs such as Felele, Adankolo, Otokiti and Ganaja. The town is situated in the tropical wet and dry savanna climate zone of Nigeria, and temperatures remain hot year-round. Rain begins in May and typically ends in October. Lokoja has a maximum temperature of about 37.9<span typeof="mw:Entity" id="mwxw"> </span>°C between December and April, average annual rainfall of about <span about="#mwt71" typeof="mw:Transclusion" id="mwyA" data-mw="{"parts":[{"template":{"target":{"wt":"cvt","href":"./Template:Cvt"},"params":{"1":{"wt":"1000"},"2":{"wt":"mm"},"3":{"wt":"ft"}},"i":0}}]}">1,000</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt71"> </span><span about="#mwt71">mm (3.3</span><span typeof="mw:Entity" about="#mwt71"> </span><span about="#mwt71">ft)</span> and average relative humidity of about 60% during the rainy season.<sup about="#mwt77" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-18" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-18"}}"><a href="#cite_note-18" id="mwyQ"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mwyg"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mwyw">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket" id="mwzA">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

</section><section data-mw-section-id="5" id="mwzQ" aria-labelledby="Religion_and_culture"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Religion_and_culture">Religion and culture</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Lokoja&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: Religion and culture"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p id="mwzg">Given the multi-ethnic nature of the town, there are various festivals, events and socio-cultural activities depending on the people's group. Thus, no particular group's festivals or their socio-cultural activities can be said to be the most prominent. For instance, the Agbo masquerade festival is celebrated by the Oworo people between the months of March and April every year. Other Okuns also celebrate the <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oro_Festival" title="Oro Festival" id="mwzw">Oro</a> / <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egungun" title="Egungun" id="mw0A">Egungun</a> festival while generally, the fishermen in Lokoja celebrate the Donkwo fishing festival and this also comes up in March/April. Editions of Lokoja boat regatta are held, though not regularly.<sup about="#mwt78" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-:0_7-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":":0"}}"><a href="#cite_note-:0-7" id="mw0Q"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw0g"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw0w">[</span>7<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw1A">]</span></span></a></sup></p>

<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mw1Q"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Childrens_Museum_of_Indianapolis_-_Egungun_masquerade_dance_garment.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mw1g"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Childrens_Museum_of_Indianapolis_-_Egungun_masquerade_dance_garment.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/The_Childrens_Museum_of_Indianapolis_-_Egungun_masquerade_dance_garment.jpg/250px-The_Childrens_Museum_of_Indianapolis_-_Egungun_masquerade_dance_garment.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/The_Childrens_Museum_of_Indianapolis_-_Egungun_masquerade_dance_garment.jpg/500px-The_Childrens_Museum_of_Indianapolis_-_Egungun_masquerade_dance_garment.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="514" data-file-height="768" data-file-type="bitmap" height="374" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mw1w"></a><figcaption id="mw2A">Egungun masquerade dance garment</figcaption></figure>

<p id="mw2Q">Religiously, Islam, Christianity and traditional religion exist in Lokoja. The Muslims go to their mosques for their worship while the Christians do the same in their various churches. Religious festivals include the Muslim Eids and the Christian Christmas and Easter.</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mw2g"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bishop_Crowther_LGEA_Primary_School,_First_Primary_School_in_Northern_Nigeria,_Lokoja.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mw2w"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bishop_Crowther_LGEA_Primary_School,_First_Primary_School_in_Northern_Nigeria,_Lokoja.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Bishop_Crowther_LGEA_Primary_School%2C_First_Primary_School_in_Northern_Nigeria%2C_Lokoja.jpg/250px-Bishop_Crowther_LGEA_Primary_School%2C_First_Primary_School_in_Northern_Nigeria%2C_Lokoja.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Bishop_Crowther_LGEA_Primary_School%2C_First_Primary_School_in_Northern_Nigeria%2C_Lokoja.jpg/500px-Bishop_Crowther_LGEA_Primary_School%2C_First_Primary_School_in_Northern_Nigeria%2C_Lokoja.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="4024" data-file-height="3018" data-file-type="bitmap" height="188" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mw3A"></a><figcaption id="mw3Q">Bishop Crowther LGEA Primary School in Lokoja, regarded as the first primary school in Northern Nigeria.</figcaption></figure>

<section data-mw-section-id="6" id="mw3g" aria-labelledby="Historical_and_cultural_sites"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Historical_and_cultural_sites">Historical and cultural sites</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Lokoja&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: Historical and cultural sites"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>

<p id="mw3w">Lokoja has several sites associated with the history of colonial administration, education, and traditional institutions in Nigeria. These sites include Iroon of
Liberty, the Bishop Crowther LGEA Primary School,<sup about="#mwt81" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Oyigbenu_19-0" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Oyigbenu"},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-Oyigbenu-19"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Oyigbenu-19" id="mw4A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw4Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4g">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw4w">]</span></span></a></sup> regarded as the first primary school in Northern Nigeria, the burial sites of the deposed Emirs in Kubuwa, the site known as the spot where the Royal Niger Company flag was lowered in 1900,<sup about="#mwt84" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-20" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{},"body":{"id":"mw-reference-text-cite_note-20"}}"><a href="#cite_note-20" id="mw5A"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw5Q"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5g">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw5w">]</span></span></a></sup> <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Lugard,_1st_Baron_Lugard" title="Frederick Lugard, 1st Baron Lugard" id="mw6A">Lord Lugard</a>'s rest room on <a rel="mw:WikiLink" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Patti" title="Mount Patti" id="mw6Q">Mount Patti</a>, and relics of the early colonial prison.<sup about="#mwt85" class="mw-ref reference" id="cite_ref-Oyigbenu_19-1" rel="dc:references" typeof="mw:Extension/ref" data-mw="{"name":"ref","attrs":{"name":"Oyigbenu"}}"><a href="#cite_note-Oyigbenu-19" id="mw6g"><span class="mw-reflink-text" id="mw6w"><span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7A">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket" id="mw7Q">]</span></span></a></sup></p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mw7g"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:“The_Spot,_Lokoja_—_Where_the_Royal_Niger_Company_Flag_Was_Lowered_for_Nigeria’s_Flag”_11.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mw7w"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:“The_Spot,_Lokoja_—_Where_the_Royal_Niger_Company_Flag_Was_Lowered_for_Nigeria’s_Flag”_11.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/%E2%80%9CThe_Spot%2C_Lokoja_%E2%80%94_Where_the_Royal_Niger_Company_Flag_Was_Lowered_for_Nigeria%E2%80%99s_Flag%E2%80%9D_11.jpg/250px-%E2%80%9CThe_Spot%2C_Lokoja_%E2%80%94_Where_the_Royal_Niger_Company_Flag_Was_Lowered_for_Nigeria%E2%80%99s_Flag%E2%80%9D_11.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/%E2%80%9CThe_Spot%2C_Lokoja_%E2%80%94_Where_the_Royal_Niger_Company_Flag_Was_Lowered_for_Nigeria%E2%80%99s_Flag%E2%80%9D_11.jpg/500px-%E2%80%9CThe_Spot%2C_Lokoja_%E2%80%94_Where_the_Royal_Niger_Company_Flag_Was_Lowered_for_Nigeria%E2%80%99s_Flag%E2%80%9D_11.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="3996" data-file-height="2997" data-file-type="bitmap" height="188" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mw8A"></a><figcaption id="mw8Q">The Spot — Royal Niger Company Flag Ceremony Site, Lokoja</figcaption></figure>

</section></section><section data-mw-section-id="7" id="mw9g" aria-labelledby="Markets"><div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Markets">Markets</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Lokoja&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: Markets"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb" id="mw9w"><a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Morning_sojourn_at_the_market_place.jpg" class="mw-file-description" id="mw-A"><img resource="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Morning_sojourn_at_the_market_place.jpg" src="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Morning_sojourn_at_the_market_place.jpg/250px-Morning_sojourn_at_the_market_place.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Morning_sojourn_at_the_market_place.jpg/500px-Morning_sojourn_at_the_market_place.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail 2x" data-file-width="2560" data-file-height="1920" data-file-type="bitmap" height="188" width="250" class="mw-file-element" id="mw-Q"></a><figcaption id="mw-g">Market place in Lokoja</figcaption></figure>
<p id="mw-w">Lokoja has three major markets: New Market (International Market), Old Market and Kpata Market. Kpata Market and New Market have their market day every Five Days. The essential products sold in these markets are grains, vegetables and general household item.</p>
